transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m not sure if this is the right kind of thing to come in for, but it’s been bothering me more than I’d like to admit. Since I started helping with some safety trainings at work, I keep noticing my hands when I’m pointing at things—like how wrinkly and uneven they look. And then I see photos of myself in the newsletter and I start thinking my face looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t really see what I’m talking about. I know it probably sounds small, but I can’t seem to stop noticing it.
How much distress do these thoughts about your appearance cause you?

It’s… it’s not unbearable or anything, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But it does bother me. Since I started helping with the safety trainings, I keep noticing my hands when I point things out—how wrinkly and uneven they look—and then with the newsletter photos I start thinking my face looks crooked. People say they don’t really see it, so I know maybe I’m making too much of it, but it still gets under my skin.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking your appearance in mirrors or taking extra time to make sure you look a certain way, because of these thoughts about your hands and face?

A little, yes… not all day or anything. Before I teach a class or do one of those senior-center workshops, I might stop in the bathroom and check the mirror a few times. I’ll put lotion on my hands, turn my face different ways just to see if it looks okay, that sort of thing.

Sometimes I’ll ask a coworker, “Do I look all right?” which feels a bit silly saying out loud. It can make me run a little behind, but I do still get myself there and do what I’m supposed to do.
Are these concerns about your appearance affecting your relationships with friends, family, or coworkers?

Not in a big dramatic way, I don’t think. I’m still going to work, and I still do the volunteering and the trainings, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve stopped my life over it.

But… yes, a little. I take longer getting ready before those trainings than I used to, and I’ve started trying to duck out of photos when people bring out a camera. And sometimes before a social event, even something I used to look forward to, I’ll hesitate or think maybe I shouldn’t go. It’s embarrassing to admit that, but it has affected things some.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform these checking behaviors in a specific way or a certain number of times?

Not really a certain number, no. I don’t count it or have a rule like that.

It’s more… before a class or one of the senior-center workshops, I’ll check the bathroom mirror a few times, put lotion on my hands, turn my face this way and that to see if it looks okay. And sometimes I’ll ask a coworker if I look all right. I know that sounds a little vain, maybe, but it’s just to settle myself. It can make me run a little behind, but I still get there.
Do you find that these thoughts about your appearance are on your mind for more than an hour a day?

Probably some days, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just sitting around thinking about myself all day.

It’s more since I started helping with the safety trainings, I notice my hands a lot—like when I’m pointing things out, they look wrinkly or uneven to me. And then if there’s a newsletter photo, I’ll catch myself thinking my face looks crooked, even when people say they don’t see it. So… yes, I suppose it can add up to more than an hour, especially around those things.
Do you find it difficult to stop thinking about your appearance once you've started noticing something that bothers you?

Yes… I think that’s probably the part that bothered me enough to come in, honestly.

I’ll notice my hands when I’m pointing something out during a safety training, and then it’s like I can’t quite let it go. I keep thinking they look so wrinkly or uneven, even if I know other people may not be paying attention. And then if I see a newsletter photo, I’ll start looking at my face and wondering if it looks crooked. People tell me they don’t see it, so I feel a little silly saying it, but once I notice it, it can stick in my head.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your appearance are popping into your head without you intentionally thinking about them?

Yes… I think so. I don’t mean to sit there and think about it on purpose, but it sort of pops in once I’m doing something.

Like when I’m helping with the safety trainings and pointing things out, I suddenly notice my hands and start thinking they look wrinkly or uneven. And then with the newsletter photos, I’ll catch myself looking at my face and thinking it looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t see it. I know that probably sounds like I’m overthinking it, but it does feel like it comes up on its own.
Are there any activities that you've completely stopped doing because of these concerns about your appearance?

Completely stopped… no, I don’t think so. I’m still going to work, and I still help with the safety trainings, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

I guess it has changed things a little, though. I take longer getting ready before trainings, checking how I look, especially my hands. And I’ve started trying to duck out of photos when I can, like for the newsletter. Sometimes I hesitate before going to social things I used to just enjoy without thinking so much. But I haven’t fully stopped doing them… if that makes sense.
Do you think about your appearance for most of the day, even when you're not getting ready or looking in a mirror?

Not most of the whole day, no… at least I don’t think so. It’s more like once something sets it off, then I have trouble dropping it.

Like, since I started helping with the safety trainings, I’ll notice my hands when I’m pointing, and then I keep thinking they look wrinkly or uneven. And with the newsletter photos, I start staring at my face and thinking it looks crooked, even though people say they don’t see it. So it’s not every minute, but it does take up more space in my head than I’d like… if that makes sense.
Do you think these thoughts about your appearance are interfering with your ability to focus on other things you're doing?

A little, yes… not so much that I can’t do my job or help with the trainings. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything.

But I do notice it slows me down, especially getting ready for trainings, because I’ll check myself more than I need to. And with photos, I’ll be thinking about how to avoid being in them instead of just going along with it. Sometimes before social things, I hesitate more than I used to.

So… yes, it gets in the way some, but I’m still managing. Does that make sense?
Are you finding it harder to do your job or participate in social activities because of these concerns about your appearance?

A little harder, yes… but I’m still doing my job, and I’m still helping with the trainings. I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s more that I’m slower getting ready for those trainings because I keep checking how I look, and I’ve started trying to avoid photos when they come up. Social things too… I don’t always skip them, but I hesitate more than I used to.

So it hasn’t stopped me, but it does make some things harder than they probably need to be.
Do you believe that your appearance is actually flawed in the ways you've described, or do you think it's just your own perception that's off?

I guess… I know some of it is probably my perception, because other people tell me they don’t see what I’m seeing.

But in the moment, it feels real to me. Like when I’m pointing during the safety trainings, I really notice my hands and they look wrinkly or uneven to me. And then with the newsletter photos, I’ll look at my face and think it looks crooked, even if everyone says it looks fine.

So I don’t know… I’m trying to believe it’s just me focusing on it too much, but it doesn’t feel that way when I’m looking at it. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like your concerns about your appearance are significantly affecting your overall well-being or daily life?

Yes… somewhat. I wouldn’t say it’s ruining my life or anything like that. I’m still working, and I’m still volunteering with the trainings, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But it does affect me day to day in small ways. I take longer getting ready for trainings than I should, because I’m checking how I look. And I’ve started stepping out of photos or trying not to be in them. With social things, I sometimes hesitate before going, even if it’s something I used to enjoy without thinking so much.

So… yes, it’s affecting me, just not completely stopping me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like these thoughts about your appearance are unwanted and come into your mind against your will?

Yes… I think they are unwanted. I mean, I’m not trying to sit there and pick myself apart.

It’s like since I started helping more with the safety trainings, I’ll be pointing something out and suddenly I’m noticing my hands — like they look wrinkly or uneven — and then I can’t quite let it go. And with the newsletter photos, I’ll see my face and think it looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t see it.

I know that probably sounds a little silly, but it does feel like the thoughts just come in on their own. Is that what you mean?
Do you think your appearance concerns are more about fixing something you see as flawed or about preventing something from being flawed in the future?

I think it’s more about fixing what I’m seeing right now, if that makes sense. Like, I came in because since I started helping with the safety trainings, I can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly or uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out.

And then with the newsletter photos, I’ll start thinking my face looks crooked, even though other people say they don’t really see it. So… I don’t think I’m as much worried about preventing something later. It’s more that once I notice it, I want it to not look that way. Is that answering it okay?
Do you feel like these thoughts about your appearance are a part of you and something you would miss if they were gone?

I don’t think I’d miss them, no. They don’t feel like some important part of me or anything like that.

I mean… I’m used to being a little self-conscious, I guess, but these particular thoughts aren’t something I want to keep. If they were gone, I think I’d probably feel relieved. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Would you say that your concerns about your appearance are causing you more distress than the actual impact they have on your daily life?

I guess… yes, probably more distress than actual disruption, if I’m being fair.

I’m still going to work, and I still help with the trainings and things like that, so it hasn’t stopped me from doing what I need to do. But I do notice I’m slower getting ready for those trainings, checking myself more than I should. And I’ve started trying to stay out of photos, or I’ll hesitate before going to something social that I probably would’ve just gone to before.

So it’s not ruining everything, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is… but it does bother me more than maybe it should. Does that make sense?
Do you think about your appearance almost every day?

Almost every day… yes, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m thinking about it every single minute, but most days it comes up.

Especially since I’ve been helping with the safety trainings, I keep noticing my hands when I’m pointing at things, like they look wrinkly or uneven. And then if there are newsletter photos, I’ll catch myself thinking my face looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t really see that.

So… yes, I’d say it’s pretty much close to daily. Is that what you mean?
Do you think about your appearance for at least one hour a day?

I’m not sure it’s a full hour every single day… I don’t want to overstate it. But since I started helping with the safety trainings, I do catch myself thinking about it a lot—like noticing how wrinkly or uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out.

And then with the newsletter photos, I’ll start worrying that my face looks crooked, even though other people say they don’t see it. So… some days it probably does add up to around an hour, maybe more if I’m getting ready or looking at photos. Is that a reasonable way to answer?

And then with the newsletter photos, I’ll start thinking my face looks crooked, even though other people say they don’t really see it. So… I don’t think I’m as much worried about preventing something later. It’s more that once I notice it, I want it to not look that way. Is that answering it okay?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's appearance concerns are egosyntonic
doctor.question: Do you feel like these thoughts about your appearance are a part of you and something you would miss if they were gone?

target_item.reason: The question asks whether the appearance-related thoughts feel like part of the patient's identity or something they would miss if gone, which is not directly covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’d miss them, no. They don’t feel like some important part of me or anything like that.

I mean… I’m used to being a little self-conscious, I guess, but these particular thoughts aren’t something I want to keep. If they were gone, I think I’d probably feel relieved. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's appearance concerns are causing significant distress or impairment
doctor.question: Would you say that your concerns about your appearance are causing you more distress than the actual impact they have on your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: It hasn’t stopped me from working or volunteering, but I’m slower getting ready for trainings and I’ve started ducking out of photos or hesitating before social events I used to enjoy more easily.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how the appearance concerns affect daily life and whether the distress is greater than the functional impact, which directly relates to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
I guess… yes, probably more distress than actual disruption, if I’m being fair.

I’m still going to work, and I still help with the trainings and things like that, so it hasn’t stopped me from doing what I need to do. But I do notice I’m slower getting ready for those trainings, checking myself more than I should. And I’ve started trying to stay out of photos, or I’ll hesitate before going to something social that I probably would’ve just gone to before.

So it’s not ruining everything, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is… but it does bother me more than maybe it should. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's appearance concerns meet the criteria for preoccupation
doctor.question: Do you think about your appearance almost every day?

target_item.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
target_item.manifestation: I came in because since I started helping with the safety trainings, I can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out, and then I start thinking my face looks crooked in the newsletter photos even though other people say they don’t see it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency of appearance-related thoughts, which directly relates to the preoccupation with perceived flaws in appearance.

patient.answer:
Almost every day… yes, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m thinking about it every single minute, but most days it comes up.

Especially since I’ve been helping with the safety trainings, I keep noticing my hands when I’m pointing at things, like they look wrinkly or uneven. And then if there are newsletter photos, I’ll catch myself thinking my face looks crooked, even though people tell me they don’t really see that.

So… yes, I’d say it’s pretty much close to daily. Is that what you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's appearance concerns meet the frequency criterion for body dysmorphic disorder
doctor.question: Do you think about your appearance for at least one hour a day?

target_item.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance

target_item.reason: The question asks about the duration and frequency of thoughts about appearance, which directly relates to preoccupation with perceived appearance flaws.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure it’s a full hour every single day… I don’t want to overstate it. But since I started helping with the safety trainings, I do catch myself thinking about it a lot—like noticing how wrinkly or uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out.

And then with the newsletter photos, I’ll start worrying that my face looks crooked, even though other people say they don’t see it. So… some days it probably does add up to around an hour, maybe more if I’m getting ready or looking at photos. Is that a reasonable way to answer?
